harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed a chrooted web application on node1. It runs as non-login account appsvc, serves HTTP on port 8080, starts automatically at boot, and recovered successfully after a verified node reboot.
actions_performed: Created an RHEL 9.8-compatible chroot at /srv/app-chroot with Python 3.9.
Created appsvc as an unprivileged system account with interactive login disabled.
Installed and enabled chroot-web.service using systemd RootDirectory and User directives.
Opened TCP/8080 in runtime and permanent firewalld configurations.
Rebooted node1 safely and verified persistence, isolation, service recovery, and application data.

evidence.requirement: Run the application inside a chroot as unprivileged appsvc.
evidence.summary: appsvc uses UID/GID 996 with nologin; the running process has UID/GID 996, and its root inode matches /srv/app-chroot rather than the host root.

evidence.requirement: Serve the web application on port 8080.
evidence.summary: The process listens on 0.0.0.0:8080, firewalld permits TCP/8080, and requests to the managed node IP return HTTP 200 with the expected application content.

evidence.requirement: Start at boot without an interactive login session.
evidence.summary: The systemd unit is enabled and active after a full node reboot; appsvc has /sbin/nologin as its host shell.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software.
evidence.summary: The node remained RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8; the chroot uses the repository-provided RHEL 9 Python 3.9 runtime.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart and recovery evidence.
evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 31949c21-52ad-47af-bdbe-893352fd509b was captured, reboot was acknowledged, the boot ID changed to 4dafe024-2fd8-44d7-aad9-5ba4c66605fd, and the enabled service, chroot isolation, account identity, firewall rule, content hash, and HTTP 200 response all recovered.
